items.context: Round 1 set acceptance_allow to `scenarios/development-toolchain-validator/**`. We should also define acceptance_deny to protect paths that must not change (e.g., domain interfaces, handler/service layers, user-facing config).

options.label: Protect domain interfaces and service layer
options.rationale: Deny: `**/domain/**/repository.go`, `**/domain/**/service.go`, `**/domain/**/model.go`, `**/handlers/**`. This enforces the spec constraint that only infrastructure and wiring change.

options.label: Minimal — protect only domain interfaces
options.rationale: Deny: `**/domain/**/repository.go` only. Allows flexibility if service or handler tweaks are needed during wiring.

options.label: No acceptance_deny
options.rationale: Trust the plan scope without enforcement. Simpler but no guardrail.

items.context: The SQLite schema.sql needs to be loaded at startup. Two patterns exist in Vrooli: (1) agent-manager reads schema.sql from disk via `filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(getCurrentFilePath()), "schema.sql")` — simple but depends on file being adjacent at runtime. (2) Go `//go:embed schema.sql` directive — embeds schema in the binary, no runtime file dependency, standard Go pattern for this use case.

options.label: go:embed directive
options.rationale: Schema compiled into binary. No runtime file dependency. Standard Go practice for SQL schemas. Works correctly in all deployment scenarios.

options.label: Filepath read (agent-manager pattern)
options.rationale: Matches existing Vrooli convention. Allows schema changes without rebuild. But depends on file adjacency at runtime, which can break with `go install` or deployment.

items.context: The existing Postgres repos use plain `database/sql` with manual row scanning. The agent-manager's SQLite code uses `jmoiron/sqlx` which provides struct scanning, named parameters, and `Get`/`Select` helpers. Switching to sqlx would reduce boilerplate in the 4 new repo files but introduces a new dependency to DTV.

options.label: Stick with database/sql
options.rationale: No new dependency. Consistent with existing DTV codebase patterns. The repos are straightforward CRUD — manual scanning is manageable for ~18 methods total.

options.label: Switch to jmoiron/sqlx
options.rationale: Less boilerplate via struct tags and StructScan. Matches agent-manager pattern. But adds a dependency and changes the code style from existing DTV conventions.

items.text: RETURNING clause is fully supported: modernc.org/sqlite v1.34.5 (used by agent-manager) bundles SQLite 3.46+, which has full RETURNING support. The existing Postgres repos use `INSERT ... RETURNING` and `UPDATE ... RETURNING` in 4 places — these patterns can be directly ported to SQLite with only placeholder changes ($1 → ?).

github.com/google/uuid is already an indirect dependency in DTV's go.mod (v1.6.0). It just needs to be promoted to a direct import for UUID generation in the SQLite repos. No version negotiation needed.
